theme: ब्रह्म, अध्यात्म, कर्म और देहांत का प्रश्न | Brahman, Ātman, karma, and the threshold of death
context: Arjuna now asks Krishna to define the terms he introduced in the previous chapter. He wants clarity about the highest reality, the self, action, the elemental plane, and the divine plane. This is not a random philosophical list; it is a practical question about how one lives and how one departs. Krishna will answer in a way that links doctrine to consciousness at the moment of death.
contextHindi: अर्जुन अब भगवान् से उन शब्दों का अर्थ पूछते हैं, जिनका कृष्ण ने पिछले अध्याय में उल्लेख किया था। वह ब्रह्म, अध्यात्म, कर्म, अधिभूत और अधिदैव का भेद समझना चाहते हैं। यह केवल तर्क नहीं, जीवन और मृत्यु के क्षण में मन की दिशा को समझने का प्रश्न है।
sanskritDevanagari:
अर्जुन उवाच |
किं तद् ब्रह्म किमध्यात्मं किं कर्म पुरुषोत्तम |
अधिभूतं च किं प्रोक्तमधिदैवं किमुच्यते ||८-१||
transliteration:
arjuna uvāca .
kiṃ tad brahma kimadhyātmaṃ kiṃ karma puruṣottama .
adhibhūtaṃ ca kiṃ proktamadhidaivaṃ kimucyate ||8-1||

wordByWord.meaning: That; referring to Brahman about which Arjuna asks.
The Absolute, the imperishable ultimate reality; in Hindi, परम सत्य, सर्वव्यापी और अविनाशी.
One’s own nature; svabhāva, as Krishna defines it in 8.3.
Visarga: the offering or act that brings about the manifestation of beings, as Krishna defines it in 8.3.
The elemental-material dimension, the field of nature and matter that supports embodied life.
Purusha, or the soul; Krishna identifies this as Adhidaiva in 8.4.

spokenHindi: अर्जुन भगवान् कृष्ण से पाँच प्रश्न पूछते हैं। वे जानना चाहते हैं कि ब्रह्म क्या है, अध्यात्म क्या है, कर्म क्या है, अधिभूत किसे कहते हैं और अधिदैव क्या है। वे कृष्ण को पुरुषोत्तम कहकर संबोधित करते हैं। इस श्लोक में अर्जुन इन शब्दों के अर्थ पूछते हैं; कृष्ण का उत्तर अभी नहीं आया है। पिछले अध्याय के अंत में कृष्ण ने कुछ ऐसे शब्दों का प्रयोग किया था। टिप्पणी के अनुसार, अर्जुन अब उन्हीं का अर्थ स्पष्ट करना चाहते हैं। इसलिए यहाँ प्रश्नों को ध्यान से सुनना ज़रूरी है। इनके उत्तर अगले श्लोकों में मिलेंगे। गीता में इन शब्दों के अर्थ समझने से पहले, हमें अर्जुन के प्रश्न और कृष्ण के उत्तर में अंतर रखना चाहिए। यह श्लोक किसी मरते हुए व्यक्ति से कोई अपेक्षा नहीं रखता। यह अर्जुन की जिज्ञासा को सामने रखता है। हम भी कठिन शब्द मिलने पर उनका अर्थ पूछ सकते हैं। बिना जल्दबाज़ी किए, एक-एक प्रश्न समझ सकते हैं।
clearEnglish: Arjuna's repeated question, “What is it?”, slows the discussion down at precisely the point where technical language could create an illusion of understanding. He asks Krishna about Brahman, adhyatma, karma, adhibhuta, and adhidaiva. These are questions about terms Krishna has already introduced; this verse does not supply their definitions. The respectful address Purushottama expresses trust without preventing inquiry. The supplied commentary explains that Arjuna wants clarification of the philosophical terms used at the end of the preceding chapter. We should therefore listen to the question as a question, rather than insert a complete metaphysical system into it. A useful contemporary inference concerns the quality of learning: repeating an impressive word is different from knowing what a speaker means by it. Before agreeing with a spiritual claim, we can ask for its context and definition. This does not require rejecting devotion. Arjuna's example shows an engaged student bringing uncertainty into a conversation with the teacher he respects.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse asks what Brahman, Adhyatma, karma, Adhibhuta, and Adhidaiva are. It does not define them here or state that they are practical categories for understanding lived reality.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: A modern learning application is to ask what technical terms mean before treating them as understood. The verse does not itself establish a hierarchy of realities or define a conditioned self.

interpretationPerspectives.label: COMMENTARY — Sri Swami Sivananda
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The DLS commentary says that Krishna used certain philosophical terms in the last two verses of the seventh discourse and that Arjuna asks about their meanings.

practicalApplication.label: Clarify one term
practicalApplication.text: Choose one unfamiliar word in a spiritual discussion. Write the speaker's question or definition and distinguish it from your assumptions.

reflectionQuestion: Which of Arjuna's five terms would I most like to understand clearly?
